literal: Is it an elixir, indeed, flesh-cherishing life, great dignity's honor to be destroyed when it has come?
translation: When great dignity and honor are destroyed, is a life that merely cherishes the physical body an elixir of immortality?
modern: தமது பெருமையும் மானமும் அழியும்படியான நிலை வந்தபோது, உடம்பை மட்டும் காப்பாற்றி வாழும் வாழ்க்கை என்ன சாகா வரம் தரும் மருந்தா?
explanation: This couplet questions the value of clinging to physical survival at the cost of one's honor. The word 'ஊன்' (flesh) emphasizes the mere physical body, contrasting it with 'பெருந்தகைமை பீடு' (the honor of great dignity). The poet asks rhetorically if a life that merely protects the flesh is an elixir of immortality ('மருந்தோ'). It implies that since the body will eventually die anyway, sacrificing one's honor just to prolong physical existence is foolish and unworthy of a noble person.
